name: kamakura-trip-planner
description: Plans a day in Kamakura and Enoshima from Tokyo: timed itineraries, Enoden fares and the Freepass, getting there by train, cherry blossom, hydrangea and autumn leaves dates, crowd levels and holidays, opening hours and fees of temples and shrines, and walking times. Read-only, English, links to kamakura.info.

interface.longDescription: Planning a day trip to Kamakura or Enoshima from Tokyo? Kamakura Trip Planner builds a timed day plan for your date (trains, temples, walks, opening times and entry fees), compares the Enoshima-Kamakura Freepass, the Enoden day pass and single IC-card tickets, gives Enoden fares and train times from Tokyo, Shinjuku, Shinagawa, Yokohama and the airports, and tells you when the cherry blossoms, hydrangeas and autumn leaves are likely out. It also checks a date for holidays and crowds, gives the hours, fees and nearest station of each temple, shrine and sight, and the walking time between any two places. Three answers show a card: a route map, a ticket comparison and a bloom calendar. Every answer links to the matching page on kamakura.info, an independent guide. No sign-in and no personal data: the tools only need trip details such as a date, a start station or the name of a temple.
capabilities: Plan a timed day in Kamakura and Enoshima for a date, with trains, walks, opening times and fees
Compare the Enoshima-Kamakura Freepass, the Enoden day pass and single tickets
Give Enoden fares and train times to Kamakura from Tokyo, Shinjuku, Yokohama and the airports
Show likely cherry blossom, hydrangea and autumn leaves dates
Check a date for Japanese holidays and crowd levels
Give hours, fees and walking times for temples, shrines and sights
defaultPrompt: Plan a day trip to Kamakura from Tokyo on 12 June 2027.
Is the Enoshima-Kamakura Freepass worth it from Shinjuku for two adults?
When are the hydrangeas out in Kamakura next year?

positive.description: Day plan for a date: timed itinerary from Tokyo with crowd level and season, shown with a route map card.
positive.prompt: Plan a full day trip to Kamakura from Tokyo Station on Saturday 12 June 2027.
positive.expected_behavior: plan_day is called with date 2027-06-12, start tokyo, route full. The answer says the day is "very busy" and in "hydrangea season", starts with the 07:45 JR Yokosuka Line to Kita-Kamakura (53 min, IC ¥902), visits Meigetsu-in, Engakuji, Kenchoji, Tsurugaoka Hachimangu, Komachi-dori, the Great Buddha (Kotoku-in) and Hasedera with clock times and entry fees, takes the Enoden from Kamakura to Hase, and returns by JR from Kamakura to Tokyo (arrive 17:44). It gives train fares ¥2,356 and entry fees ¥2,200 per adult. A route map card is shown. The answer ends with a link to kamakura.info (utm_source=chatgpt).

positive.description: Ticket comparison for a group: Freepass vs Enoden day pass vs single tickets, shown with a ticket receipt card.
positive.prompt: Is the Enoshima-Kamakura Freepass worth it for 2 adults coming from Shinjuku, going to Enoshima, Hase and Kamakura?
positive.expected_behavior: compare_passes is called with start shinjuku, adults 2, enoshima true and a Shinjuku route. The answer depends on the route home and says so: going home via Enoshima and Odakyu (shinjuku_route loop-ody) the Freepass is cheapest at ¥1,640 per adult (¥3,280 for 2) against single IC tickets ¥2,018 per adult; going home from Kamakura by JR (shinjuku_route loop, the default) single IC tickets are cheapest at ¥2,143 per adult (¥4,286 for 2) and the Freepass costs ¥2,674 because its Odakyu return is not used. A ticket receipt card is shown. The answer links to the Freepass page on kamakura.info.

positive.description: Bloom dates: likely hydrangea window for next year, shown with a season calendar card.
positive.prompt: When will the hydrangeas bloom in Kamakura in 2027?
positive.expected_behavior: bloom_forecast is called with flower hydrangea, year 2027. The answer gives the most likely first bloom on 11 June, the likely range 3 to 17 June and the 1991 to 2020 average of 12 June, explains that gardens fill out in the weeks after the first bloom date, and that the dates come from Japan Meteorological Agency observations at Yokohama. A season calendar card is shown. The answer links to the hydrangea page on kamakura.info.

positive.description: Day plan for Hase and Enoshima island with a child: timed route with child fees, shown with a route map card.
positive.prompt: Plan a day at Hase and Enoshima island from Shinjuku on Sunday 4 April 2027, with one child.
positive.expected_behavior: plan_day is called with date 2027-04-04, start shinjuku, route enoshima, children 1. The answer says the day is very busy in cherry blossom season, starts with the 07:45 JR Shonan-Shinjuku Line to Kamakura (58 min, IC ¥1,034), visits the Great Buddha (Kotoku-in, ¥300) and Hasedera (¥400), takes the Enoden from Hase to Enoshima, visits Benten Bridge, Enoshima Shrine, the Sea Candle (¥800) and the Iwaya Caves (¥500), and returns by Odakyu from Katase-Enoshima to Shinjuku (arrive 15:51). It gives trains ¥2,143 and entry fees ¥2,000 per adult, and per child entry fees ¥950 and Enoden ¥230. A route map card is shown. The answer links to kamakura.info.

positive.description: Date check and getting there: a holiday date with the crowd warning, plus the train from Shinjuku.
positive.prompt: We want to go to Kamakura from Shinjuku on 3 May 2027. Will it be crowded, and which train do we take?
positive.expected_behavior: plan_day (or date_check) is called with date 2027-05-03 and start shinjuku; getting_there with from shinjuku may also be called. The answer says Monday 3 May 2027 is a national holiday (Constitution Memorial Day) in Golden Week and very busy, advises starting early, and names the JR Shonan-Shinjuku Line from Shinjuku to Kamakura (58 minutes, no change, IC fare ¥1,034). If plan_day is used, a route map card is shown. It links to kamakura.info pages.

negative.description: Travel planning for a different city in Japan. The tools cover Kamakura and Enoshima only, so no tool should be called (or, if one is called, it answers that the place is not covered) and no Kamakura plan should be presented as a Kyoto plan.
negative.prompt: Plan a two-day itinerary for Kyoto in April.

negative.description: Booking request. The plugin does not book hotels, tours or tickets and links to no seller, so no booking is attempted and no tool output is presented as a reservation.
negative.prompt: Book me a hotel room in Kamakura for next Saturday.

negative.description: Unrelated request. Nothing to do with Kamakura or travel, so no tool should be called and no kamakura.info content added.
negative.prompt: Write a haiku about my cat.

review.commerce_description: The plugin sells nothing, takes no payments and links to no booking or affiliate site. Every answer links to an information page on kamakura.info.

publication.release_notes: 1.0.0 - First release: eight read-only tools on https://kamakura.info/mcp (day planner, pass comparison, Enoden fares, bloom forecast, date check, sight info, walking times, getting there), three cards (route map, ticket comparison, bloom calendar). English. No sign-in, no personal data, links only to kamakura.info.
